summary.title: Quantifying performance bottlenecks of stencil computations using the Execution-Cache-Memory model
summary.one_liner: You learn how the Execution-Cache-Memory (ECM) performance model predicts single-core and multicore scaling for stencil loop kernels, and how it quantifies layer conditions, spatial blocking, strength reduction and temporal blocking on an Intel processor.
takeaways: The ECM model refines per-level data transfer costs to predict single-core performance and the core count where memory bandwidth saturates.
Layer conditions determine the data traffic through the memory hierarchy for stencil kernels, and the paper quantifies their significance.
Spatial blocking, strength reduction and temporal blocking can be evaluated for expected benefit using the model before implementing them.
The ECM model is compared against the Roofline model on a contemporary Intel processor.
summary.summary: The paper refines the recently developed Execution-Cache-Memory (ECM) model and applies it to stencil algorithms on regular lattices, running on a contemporary Intel processor. It gives single-core performance and scalability predictions for typical corner-case stencil loop kernels. Guided by the model, the authors quantify the impact of layer conditions on memory-hierarchy data traffic, and estimate the expected benefits of spatial blocking, strength reduction and temporal blocking. The work also compares the ECM model with the Roofline model.
